title: Podatność koła pod geometrycznym bodźcem statycznej drogi
question: Czy wheel-local contact Hertz zmniejsza transfer przyspieszenia z nieruchomej geometrii drogi do masy resorowanej bez zmiany topologii kontaktu, klasy static-contact ani zachowania stycznego?
hypothesis: Pośredni zakres lokalnej podatności obniży RMS i peak odpowiedzi nadwozia na kontrolowany bump statycznej drogi, zachowując ciągłość kontaktu, ograniczoną kompresję statyczną i podobny bilans energii.

locked_factors.wheel_geometry: identical b3Wheel profile, cornerRadius, mass and inertia
locked_factors.manifold_topology: strict rigid support and unchanged feature IDs
locked_factors.contact_damping_ratio: world value during the Hertz sweep
locked_factors.ground_contact_class: static road geometry; no kinematic ground body
locked_factors.road_profile: one frozen analytic bump profile represented by at least two declared mesh resolutions; traversal speed is identical
locked_factors.quarter_car: same sprung/unsprung masses, suspension and initial pose
locked_factors.traversal_mechanism: static road stays static; vehicle motion method must pass flat-road parity and must not inject vertical constraint work
locked_factors.sampling_contract: frame and substep sampling rates are declared; peak metrics require temporal-convergence evidence

confounds: A kinematic road body uses dynamic-contact softness and is not equivalent to JV static terrain.
A direct force pulse calibrates compliance but does not measure geometric road-input comfort.
Changing bump shape, speed or suspension together with Hertz would destroy attribution.
Teleporting the road or vehicle can inject discontinuities that masquerade as tire response.
Retuning steering or suspension before the wheel decision can hide the measured transfer.
A C2 analytic profile becomes piecewise planar after triangulation; a result that changes with mesh resolution is facet filtering, not tire compliance.
A kinematic carriage or towing constraint can inject vertical work; flat-road parity must prove neutral traversal before the bump sweep.
Solver totalNormalImpulse is not automatically physical force or work; its conversion must be calibrated against known static load before interpretation.
Frame-level peaks can alias substep transients; the effect must survive temporal-resolution convergence.
Zero is an inheritance sentinel and cannot represent true zero damping; damping sweeps require a separate activation contract.
The shape-wide override affects every b3Wheel contact, including dynamic obstacles; Q2R only validates static-road transfer.

levels.rig: headless quarter-car translated over a frozen static bump mesh
levels.purpose: Measure road-to-wheel-to-chassis transfer while preserving the same static contact class as JV terrain.
levels.entry_gate: Published WHEEL-SOFT-03 Q2 result exists; static-road rig proves identical input trace and zero topology drift.
levels.exit_gate: Three fresh repeats per variant, finite metrics, exact road-input hash, zero gaps/topology drift and predeclared compression/energy guardrails.

levels.rig: full JV vehicle over the same static bump contract
levels.purpose: Transfer only candidates supported by Q2R without retuning the vehicle.
levels.entry_gate: Q2R has a sealed SUPPORTED or STRONGLY_SUPPORTED decision.
levels.exit_gate: Effect sign repeats in the full vehicle and no steering/contact regression appears.

metrics: analytic road profile hash, mesh-resolution id and sampled input trace hash
flat-road parity: vertical acceleration, energy drift, speed drift and topology before any bump run
wheel and chassis vertical acceleration rms/peak with temporal-convergence comparison
calibrated normal load plus solver impulse diagnostic; work from explicit energy accounting
contact gaps, point count and feature-ID persistence
promotion_rules: The analytic road input and traversal trace must be byte-identical between variants and fresh processes.
Effect sign and approximate magnitude must agree across at least two mesh resolutions of the same analytic profile.
Traversal must pass flat-road parity before any bump result is admissible.
Peak conclusions require a declared temporal-convergence check; frame-only peaks are not sufficient.
A candidate with topology drift, contact gaps, non-finite metrics or excessive static compression cannot advance.
Q2R is interpreted by paired repeats; the runner never selects a winner automatically.
Q3 may receive at most baseline plus two Q2R-supported candidates.
No shipping vehicle defaults change inside this experiment.
manual_gates: Jozz reviews only candidates that pass Q2R and checks for visible sinking, delayed rebound or sticky contact in Q3.
A subjective feeling difference is recorded separately from technical guardrail failures.
blockers: Implement a static-road Q2R runner without kinematic-ground contact-class drift.
Freeze and hash one analytic bump profile at two mesh resolutions, traversal speed and motion trace.
Prove flat-road parity for the traversal mechanism before executing bump variants.
Calibrate impulse/load semantics and add temporal-convergence telemetry.
Add an adapter that validates repeated-world agreement, input identity, topology and guardrails before immutable execution.
